newsitem.title: USA: Equity Residential to buy Wellsford.
newsitem.headline: Equity Residential to buy Wellsford.

text.p: Equity Residential Properties Trust and Wellsford Residential Property Trust said Friday they had agreed to merge in a deal that would fold Wellsford into Equity Residential.
The deal values Wellsford at about $1 billion, or $29.61 per share, an 18.7 percent premium over its current stock price, the companies said.
Equity Residential is owned by Samuel Zell.

Each Wellsford share will be worth a tax-free 0.625 share of Equity Residential, or about $27.11, plus one share of Wellsford Properties Inc, a newly formed company that will continue Wellsford's development activities, the companies said in a joint statement.
The Wellsford Properties Inc shares are expected to have a net book value of between $2.50 and $2.75 each, partially taxed as a dividend.
The exchange ratio is subject to upward revision if Equity Residential shares fall below $40. If they drop below $37, the parties have the right to terminate the merger agreement.

Equity Residential shares closed at 43-3/8 on the NYSE on Thursday. Based on that price, Equity Residential will issue 10.7 million shares, worth $464 million, and assume Wellsford's outstanding debt of $330 million.
It will also exchange about $158 million in preferred shares. The new conversion ratio for Wellsford Series A convertible preferred shares would be 0.5544, they said.
The merger is expected to be completed by May. Approval by shareholders of both companies is required.

The combined companies will operate under the Equity Residential Properties name and will be the second-largest publicly traded U.S. REIT, with 317 properties and a market capitalization of about $5.3 billion.
